approvals.breakGlassDisabledHint: The override is switched off. A request whose approver is unreachable can only be decided by a second person.
approvals.breakGlassHint: What happens when the approver cannot be reached: after this wait, a system:root administrator may approve a request alone. The override is recorded as such in the audit log.
approvals.breakGlassMinHoursHint: The delay is the control, not an obstacle to it: it guarantees the normal two-person path had its chance first. 0 uses the default of 1 hour.
approvals.description: Require two people for irreversible operations: one requests, a different person approves, and only then does it happen. Off by default.
approvals.destructiveHint: Gating this makes every such deletion need a second person — including deleting a single message.
approvals.enabledHint: When off, every operation below behaves exactly as it did before. Nothing is queued.
approvals.expiresHint: A stale request that is approved months later would silently unfreeze data. 0 uses the default of 72 hours.
approvals.forbidden: Dual control requires the Enterprise edition and system:root or user:manage permission.
approvals.operationsHint: Only listed operations are gated. By default the requester cannot approve their own request — not even an administrator. The break-glass override below is the one exception.
approvals.retentionHint: The permanent record is the audit log; this only bounds the queue history. 0 uses the default of 365 days.
approvals.revocationHint: Gating this means a token cannot be revoked until a second person approves — including a user revoking their own leaked token.
approvals.title: Dual control

compliance.title: Compliance configuration
compliance.description: Retention windows and schedule intervals for the audit trail, integrity checks and timestamp anchoring. Empty fields keep the server defaults; type a value to override.
compliance.forbidden: Compliance configuration requires the Pro or Enterprise edition and the system:root permission.
compliance.auditRetentionDaysHint: Audit records older than this are purged. 0 disables cleanup.
compliance.integrityScheduleHoursHint: A quick integrity check runs this often. 0 disables the periodic loop.
compliance.integrityRetentionDaysHint: How many days of integrity reports to keep. 0 disables cleanup.
compliance.tspIntervalHoursHint: How often content hashes are anchored with the Time-Stamp Authority.

siem.description: Forward audit events to an external SIEM (Splunk, Elasticsearch, QRadar…) as JSON signed with an HMAC-SHA256 signature.
siem.enabledHint: When enabled, matching audit events are pushed to the webhook URL.
siem.forbidden: SIEM forwarding requires the Enterprise edition and system:root or user:manage permission.
siem.formatHint: Wire format of the forwarded payload. Generic is a plain JSON envelope; Splunk HEC expects an HTTP Event Collector endpoint; Elasticsearch bulk emits NDJSON for the _bulk API.
siem.hmacSecretHint: The signature is sent in the X-Siem-Signature header as sha256=<hex> of the raw request body.
siem.mappingHint: One rule per line: set <path> = "literal" · set <path> = {{field}} · copy <from> = <to> · rename <from> = <to> · drop <path> … Paths are dotted; {{field}} interpolates the string form, a bare {{field}} copies the value as-is. Rules run top to bottom on each event.
siem.mappingPlaceholder:
set payload.host = "bichon"
rename user = actor
copy seq = event_id
drop prev_hash
siem.retryHint: Failed batches are retried with exponential backoff and are never dropped — the SIEM should deduplicate by the event seq.
siem.title: SIEM Webhook

timestampAnchor.anchorsHint: Every anchored tree root with its TSA token. The newest anchor is the current one.

timestampAnchor.notFound: No archived envelope with that ID exists, so no counter-proof can be produced.
timestampAnchor.proofHint: This email is covered by an anchored Merkle tree. Export the token and root so a third party can verify the proof independently.
timestampAnchor.proofUnanchored: This envelope exists but no anchor covers it yet — the next anchoring cycle will include it.
timestampAnchor.subtitle: Each cycle, a Merkle tree over the archived content hashes is rooted and the root is sent to an external RFC 3161 TSA, so the archive can later be proven to have existed unmodified at a certified time. One token per cycle, regardless of message volume.
timestampAnchor.title: Timestamp anchoring
